note: Lifetime limit cut to £500,000 from 6 April 2027 raises CGT on qualifying disposals; no effect before 2027-28

Carer's Allowance withdrawn £1 for £1 of weekly earnings above the £204 limit from 2030-31 instead of stopping at it: Carer's Allowance spending rises from 2030-31; no effect before. Reviewer to confirm (María) before publication
Zero VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain, 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2028: VAT receipts fall in 2026-27 (182 days) and 2027-28; nothing after
Zero employer Class 1 rate for employees aged 21 to 24 up to the upper secondary threshold from April 2027: employer NI receipts fall

Employer Class 1 secondary threshold raised from £5,000 to £9,100 a year from 6 April 2027, moving as current law's threshold does after that: employer NI receipts fall; with employers' total cost held fixed the saving goes to pay, so income tax and employee NI recover only part of it; no effect before 2027-28
Deferred fuel duty rises keep duty, and the VAT on it, lower than current law in every year from 2026-27

£100 one-off payment, winter 2026-27, to households in England in council tax bands A to D: spending rises in 2026-27 only. The Treasury's £2.6bn likely includes the devolved governments' Barnett share, which is not modelled. Reviewer to confirm (María) before publication
Plan 2 threshold rises with RPI from April 2027 instead of staying frozen: modelled repayments fall
5-point VAT cut on petrol and diesel for 121 days of 2026-27 and 61 of 2027-28: VAT receipts fall; nothing after
Personal allowance raised to the full new State Pension for people over State Pension age from 2027-28: income tax falls
Personal allowance and basic rate band held at 2030-31 values in 2031-32 instead of uprated: income tax rises in 2031-32 only (the last model year), and employee NI moves with them

Income tax rates on dividends, savings income and property income each 2 points higher from 6 April 2027, on top of current law, with incomes held fixed: income tax receipts rise in every year from 2027-28; no effect before

£100 top-up paid once, winter 2026-27, to households in Great Britain on Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit or income-related ESA, at DESNZ's receipt rates: spending rises in 2026-27 only
